fact: Pigeons are surprisingly sophisticated art critics. In a 1995 study, researchers successfully trained pigeons to tell the difference between paintings by Claude Monet and Pablo Picasso with over 90% accuracy. The birds could even correctly categorize Impressionist and Cubist styles they had never seen before.
sources: Journal of the Experimental Analysis of Behavior (Watanabe, Sakamoto, & Wakita, 1995)
hook: A pigeon might actually understand high art better than you do.
script: A pigeon might actually understand high art better than you do. Back in 1995, researchers successfully trained pigeons to tell the difference between paintings by Claude Monet and Pablo Picasso. The birds pulled it off with over ninety percent accuracy. They could even correctly categorize Impressionist and Cubist styles they had never seen before. Honestly, city birds might have better taste than most of us.
